cards.name: VR Plane to Sphere
cards.summary: Projects a flat 2D layer (title, logo, photo, inset clip) onto the inside of a 360 equirectangular sphere so it looks undistorted when the 360 video is viewed in a headset or 360 player. On a normal flat sequence it shows the clip curved and shrunk on a transparent background.
use_for: Place a lower-third or title card inside a 360 documentary so it reads flat in the viewer
Drop a flat news clip or photo as a floating screen inside 360 footage
Put a channel logo or watermark into a 360 YouTube upload without seam distortion
avoid: Using it on ordinary 16:9 projects: the output is a warped, shrunk frame that looks like an error
Pushing the plane towards the poles (large Projection Tilt, beyond about +/-45): it stretches hard in the flat equirect frame and is awkward to read in a headset
Forgetting to match Frame Layout / FOV to the 360 sequence, or the plane lands with the wrong size or doubled

params.name: Scale (Degrees)
params.does: Angular width of the projected plane on the sphere
params.typical: 30-60 for a title, 90-120 for a large floating screen

params.name: Feather
params.does: Softens the edges of the projected plane
params.typical: 0 for crisp graphics, 10-25 for photo insets

params.name: Projection Pan (Y axis)
params.does: Moves the plane left/right around the sphere (degrees); works directly, no switch needed

params.name: Projection Tilt (X axis)
params.does: Moves the plane up/down on the sphere (degrees)
params.typical: -20..20 so it stays near eye level

params.name: Frame Layout
params.does: Mono or stereo layout of the 360 sequence (dropdown)

params.name: Stereo Disparity (Degrees)
params.does: Depth offset between eyes for stereo layouts
params.typical: 0 mono; 0.5-3 to float a title in stereo

cards.equivalent: VR Plane to Sphere (After Effects Immersive Video)
cards.scripting: Apply to the graphic/inset clip on a track above the 360 footage in a 360 (2:1 equirect) sequence. Rows named "" are group-end markers: ignore. 'Rotate Source' and 'Rotate Projection' are twirl-down group headers (harvested as bools, like Lumetri's 'Basic Correction'/'Light' headers), NOT switches: do not set them; the Tilt/Pan/Roll angles under them work on their own. Angles are degrees even though the harvested clamp is +/-32768; keep them in -180..180. Which group positions the plane on the sphere (Projection) vs turns the flat source before projection (Source) follows the Adobe/Mettle docs, not a test render: verify. Frame Layout labels are from the docs, not the harvest. On a flat 1920x1080 frame the demo shows a curved, shrunken inset on black, which is the correct behaviour.

verified.note: The flat frame is projected onto the sphere and shrunk to a curved, bulging inset (about 40% of the width) on black/transparent, as the summary says for a flat sequence.

cards.name: VR Projection
cards.summary: Reprojects 360/VR footage: changes its layout (mono, over/under, side by side), field of view, and re-orients it with Pan, Tilt and Roll. Used to fit 180/360 media into a different VR sequence or to reframe where the viewer starts.
use_for: Rotate a 360 clip so the key action (speaker, stage) sits in front of the default view
Put 180-degree footage into a 360 sequence or convert stereo layouts
Level a tilted horizon in 360 interview footage
Animate Pan for a slow spherical spin in a 360 teaser
avoid: Applying to ordinary flat footage expecting a reframe: it bends and wraps the image instead
Wrong Input Layout for stereo media gives doubled or squashed images
Chaining several VR Projection / VR Rotate Sphere instances on one clip: every reprojection resamples and softens detail; do the whole reorientation in one instance

params.name: Pan
params.typical: -180..180 to bring the subject to the front

params.name: Roll
params.does: Rotates the sphere around the view axis (degrees)

cards.equivalent: VR Converter / VR Rotate Sphere (After Effects)
cards.scripting: Rows named "" or " " and NewRotationOrder are internal: ignore. Pan/Tilt/Roll are true degrees with sane clamps (-180..180, -90..90). Input/Output Projection are 0..1 dropdowns defaulting to 1 (likely equirectangular); labels unknown, leave them. Filtering 0..5 labels unknown, keep default 1 unless verified. Layout labels follow the usual Premiere VR order but are not harvested: verify. On flat 16:9 footage the demo shows a wrapped, bent picture, not a clean reframe.

verified.note: Pan 90 / Tilt 25 re-orients the frame as a sphere: subjects shift left, the image wraps with a hard vertical seam at the right and pinches toward a pole at the bottom.

cards.name: VR Rotate Sphere
cards.summary: Rotates 360 equirectangular footage around the X (tilt), Y (pan) and Z (roll) axes without seams, to set the starting view or fix a tilted horizon.
use_for: Set the front-facing direction of a 360 rally or event clip so viewers start on the stage
Level a rolled or tilted 360 camera horizon
Animate a slow pan to guide attention in a 360 explainer
avoid: Using it on flat 16:9 footage: the image wraps and bends at the edges
Fast animated rotation in 360: causes motion sickness in headsets

params.name: Frame Layout
params.does: Mono or stereo layout of the clip (dropdown)

cards.equivalent: VR Rotate Sphere (After Effects Immersive Video)
cards.scripting: Angles in degrees; harvested clamp is +/-32768 but use -180..180. Unnamed "" rows are internal: ignore. Frame Layout labels are from Mettle SkyBox docs, not harvested. Demo on a flat frame shows a shifted, wrapped and curved picture.

verified.note: Pan 90 / Tilt 20 rotates the sphere: figures shift right, right-edge content wraps in at the left, and the horizon and foreground blocks curve.

cards.name: VR Sharpen
cards.summary: Sharpens 360 equirectangular footage while treating the left/right edges as one continuous seam, so no visible line appears where the sphere wraps.
use_for: Recover detail in soft stitched 360 camera footage before upload
Add bite to 360 drone or event shots that went soft after stabilisation
avoid: Pushing Sharpen Amount high: halos and crunchy noise, worse in headsets
Using it on flat footage: Unsharp Mask or Sharpen does the same job more cheaply; only 360 media needs the seam-aware wrap
On flat (non-360) footage at high Sharpen Amount the top and bottom rows (the sphere poles) smear into saturated colour fringes: crop or scale past them
cards.scripting: Default Sharpen Amount is 0, so the effect does nothing until set. Unnamed "" row is internal. Frame Layout labels from Mettle docs, not harvested. Demo at 100 is deliberately strong to be visible; use 10-30 in real edits.

verified.note: Interior detail is clearly crisper (mean horizontal gradient 3.7 to 6.1 vs the reference), and the top, bottom and corner rows smear into saturated colour fringes.

cards.name: Vertical Flip
cards.summary: Flips the clip upside down (mirror across the horizontal axis). No settings.
use_for: Fake a water or floor reflection by stacking a flipped copy under the original with lower opacity, blur and a Crop
Disorientation beat in a trailer or satire reel (world turned upside down), ideally on a hard cut or with a whip/spin transition
Mirror-symmetry title background: top half of a shot plus a flipped copy on the bottom half (Crop both)
avoid: Footage with readable text, logos, party symbols or number plates: they read as upside-down mirror writing
Fixing a camera mounted upside down: that image is rotated 180 degrees, so Vertical Flip alone leaves it mirrored left-right; use Motion Rotation 180 (or Vertical Flip + Horizontal Flip)
Real news or political footage presented as fact: a flipped image of a real event can read as manipulation
cards.equivalent: Transform (Scale Height -100) in After Effects, or layer Scale [100, -100]
cards.scripting: No properties: apply with {"name": "Vertical Flip", "pr_props": {}}; adding the effect is the flip, so demo_settings is empty and the effect is still fully visible (validate_cards.py exempts effects with no settable properties). It has nothing to keyframe; to animate a flip use Motion/Transform Scale or Rotation, or cut it on and off.

verified.note: The whole frame is mirrored top to bottom: flowers at the top, faces and stripes upside down at the bottom.

cards.name: Wave Warp
cards.summary: Bends the image with a travelling wave (sine, square, triangle, noise and so on) that animates on its own over time. Gives a flag, water, heat-haze or wobbly-cartoon distortion.
use_for: Make a flat flag or banner graphic ripple in a political explainer
Dream or flashback transition in a documentary (ramp Wave Height up then down)
Heat-haze or underwater feel on B-roll at low height
Wobbly comic distortion on a meme or satire beat
avoid: Large heights on faces or text: looks cheap and unreadable
Edges pulling in transparent or black gaps: scale the clip up a few percent (Pinning could hold edges, but its indices are unverified)
Leaving Antialiasing at Low on detailed footage: jagged edges

params.name: Wave Type
params.typical: 0 sine for smooth ripples, 7/8 noise for haze

params.name: Wave Height
params.does: Amplitude of the distortion in pixels

params.name: Direction
params.does: Direction the waves travel (degrees, 0 = up); the image is displaced across that direction
params.typical: 90 default: waves travel left-to-right and horizontal lines ripple up/down (flag); 0/180: waves travel vertically, vertical lines wobble sideways (rising heat haze)

params.name: Wave Speed
params.does: Cycles per second the wave travels; 0 = static

params.name: Pinning
params.typical: 0 None (default); the edge options sit at other indices but the menu includes separator rows, so test-render before relying on one

params.name: Phase
params.typical: keyframe instead of speed for exact control

cards.scripting: Animates by itself from Wave Speed even without keyframes; set Wave Speed 0 for a frozen wave. Heights/widths are pixels, so scale with resolution. Wave Type and Antialiasing labels follow the After Effects menus (9 and 3 entries matching the 0..8 and 0..2 ranges, Premiere is 0-based where AE is 1-based). Pinning has 11 indices (0..10) for 9 AE labels because the menu contains separators: only 0 = None is safe; verify any other index on a test render.

verified.note: Sine waves ripple the whole image (wavy walls, foreground blocks and faces) and scallop black gaps along the top and bottom edges.

cards.name: MXF/ARRIRAW Development Settings
cards.category: Source Settings (master clip, not in Effects panel)
cards.summary: Master-clip source settings that develop ARRIRAW recorded inside MXF (ALEXA Mini LF / ALEXA 35 style): colour space, exposure index, white balance and tint applied at decode.
use_for: Fix white balance of ARRIRAW MXF footage at the raw stage before grading
Choose a log or display colour space for ARRI footage in a documentary pipeline
avoid: Applying it to anything other than ARRIRAW MXF media: it does nothing or is not available
Grading WB in Lumetri when the raw setting can fix it cleaner

params.name: White Balance
params.does: Colour temperature in kelvin used to develop the raw

params.name: Color Space
params.does: Output colour space of the decode (dropdown)
params.typical: leave default unless the colour pipeline says otherwise

params.name: Exposure Index
params.does: ISO / EI the raw is developed at (dropdown filled from the clip)

cards.equivalent: ARRIRAW source settings via Interpret Footage in After Effects
cards.scripting: Not a timeline effect: lives on the master clip (Source Settings / Master Clip effect) of an ARRIRAW MXF file, so a script must target the project item's master clip, not a sequence track item. Exposure Index harvested range is 0..0 because no ARRI clip was loaded: its options only appear with real media. White Balance harvested default 2000 is a placeholder, not the clip's metadata value. Color Space labels unknown. Low confidence on scripting reachability.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (source-settings / raw-format effect), so the gallery did not render a frame for it.

cards.name: Canon Cinema RAW Light Source Settings
cards.category: Source Settings (master clip, not in Effects panel)
cards.summary: Master-clip source settings for Canon Cinema RAW Light (.crm) footage: colour temperature, tint, exposure, colour space and gamma chosen at decode.
use_for: Rescue a stop of under/over-exposure on Canon C70/C300/R5 raw clips
Match white balance across Canon raw interview cameras before grading
Pick Canon Log vs display gamma for a documentary colour pipeline
avoid: Exposure at the extremes (+/-3): noise and clipped highlights
Mixing gamma choices across cameras in one scene: shots will not match
cards.equivalent: Camera raw interpretation in After Effects (no direct effect)
cards.scripting: Only on .crm Canon Cinema RAW Light master clips; target the project item's master clip, not a track item. Unnamed "" bool rows are internal (the first likely toggles using clip metadata vs overrides). Color Space and Gamma labels unknown: do not guess indices.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (source-settings / raw-format effect), so the gallery did not render a frame for it.

cards.name: CinemaDNG Source Settings
cards.category: Source Settings (master clip, not in Effects panel)
cards.summary: Master-clip source settings for CinemaDNG raw image sequences (Blackmagic, DJI drones): temperature, tint and exposure applied at decode.
use_for: Fix white balance on DJI or Blackmagic CinemaDNG drone shots in a documentary
Pull back highlights or lift shadows a stop before grading
avoid: Applying to non-DNG media: not available
Extreme exposure (+/-5): noise and clipping
cards.equivalent: Camera Raw (Interpret Footage) in After Effects
cards.scripting: Master-clip Source Settings for CinemaDNG sequences only; target the master clip, not a track item. Temperature default 2000 in the harvest is a placeholder, real clips load their metadata white balance. Blank-named " " (single space) bool rows are group markers: ignore.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (source-settings / raw-format effect), so the gallery did not render a frame for it.
verified.second_opinion: corrected: scripting note called the blank rows "" but the harvest names them " " (single space); not_rendered / needs_input verdict and empty demo_settings agreed

cards.name: Cineon Source Settings
cards.category: Source Settings (master clip, not in Effects panel)
cards.summary: Master-clip source settings that convert log Cineon/DPX scans to a viewable image: black/white points, gamma, highlight rolloff and log-to-linear conversion.
use_for: Normalise flat log DPX film scans or archive transfers for a documentary
Set highlight rolloff on scanned archival footage before grading
avoid: Applying to ordinary video: only Cineon/DPX files expose it
Wrong black/white points crush shadows or clip highlights

params.name: Preset
params.typical: leave default unless the lab specifies

params.name: Converted Black Point
params.does: Output level mapped from the input black

params.name: Converted White Point
params.does: Output level mapped from the input white

params.name: Highlight Rolloff
params.does: How softly highlights roll into white

params.name: Logarithmic Conversion
params.does: Converts log to linear when on

params.name: Units
params.does: Units used for the point values (dropdown 0..2)

cards.equivalent: Cineon Converter (After Effects Utility) / Interpret Footage > Cineon Settings
cards.scripting: Master-clip Source Settings for .cin/.dpx media only. Input Black Point and Input White Point harvested as 0..0 (no DPX loaded) so they cannot be set without real media. Harvested defaults (white point 0, gamma 0.01) are placeholders. Preset and Units labels unknown; typical values come from AE Cineon Converter conventions, low confidence.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (source-settings / raw-format effect), so the gallery did not render a frame for it.

cards.name: Sony Raw Source Settings

use_for: Choose a log (S-Gamut/S-Log) vs display (Rec.709) decode of Sony F65/F55 RAW before grading a trailer or documentary
avoid: Expecting it on XAVC, X-OCN/VENICE or other non-F65-family Sony files: they use other components or none
Decoding to log without a LUT or grade afterwards: the picture stays flat and grey

params.name: Color Space
